root.name: Amsterdam Attack
root.moves: 1. e3 e5 2. c4 d6 3. Nc3 Nc6 4. b3 Nf6

overview: White meets ...e5 with a slow English-type set-up: e3, c4, Nc3 and b3, aiming for Bb2 and Nf3 rather than occupying the centre. Black has a free central position with ...e5, ...d6 and ...Nc6. It is a quiet Van't Kruijs line that depends on piece play and later d4 or f4 breaks.

white_ideas.idea: Fianchetto with b3 and Bb2 against e5
Develop Nf3 and Be2, then break with d4 or f4

black_ideas.idea: Develop smoothly and aim for ...g6, ...Bg7 or ...Be7

character.notes: A slow set-up with no early forcing play, though Black has more central space.

soundness.notes: It is playable if passive; Black has a comfortable game.

structure.notes: Neither side commits the centre; White may later play d4 or f4.

approach.notes: Part of the rare 1.e3 repertoire; strong players use it seldom.

level.notes: Plans are easy but there is little theory and a tendency to drift.

character.reason: Quiet development from both sides with no clear tilt to solid or sharp.

soundness.reason: White's slow set-up is passive but fine.

structure.reason: The centre stays undecided and flank openings can transpose.

approach.reason: The 1.e3 approach is rarely chosen by strong players.

level.reason: The plans are plain but need good judgement about when to break the centre.

plans.reason: White fianchettoes and attacks e5 and d4 later.
